content.text:
The pattern matches Li₂CrO₂ (mp-1178001) alone.

- **Peak sequence:** The observed peaks are at about 18.15° (~24), 25.85° (100), 31.5° (~11), 36.7° (~9), 39.1° (~10), 41.2° (~38) and 43.4° (~20), with further peaks of ~29 and ~14 higher up. The simulated Li₂CrO₂ pattern gives the same sequence of relative intensities: 28, 100, 10, 9, 6, 40, 23, then 30 and 8.5 later.
- **Spacing:** The 41.2° and 43.4° peaks are 44 grid steps (2.2°) apart. The gap between the matching simulated peaks (40 and 23) looks about the same.
- **Peak positions not checked exactly:** I only counted grid points in the simulated pattern roughly, so I compared the sequence and spacing of peaks, not exact angles. Any small overall offset could come from strain.
- **Other candidates:**
  - The two double perovskites (Sr₂FeBiO₆ and Ba₂MgMoO₆) would put a peak near 21.6°, and the data show none there.
  - The CaV₂O₄ spinel's first peaks would fall near 17.2° and 28.3°, which don't match.
  - The simulated patterns I checked for DyVO₄, Li₃RuO₄, K₂RbLaV₂O₈, V₂Zn₂O₇ and BaCoO₃ have intensity patterns that don't match the observed one.
- **Second phase:** No clear unexplained peaks remain, so I don't see evidence of one.

{"present": ["mp-1178001"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "The observed peak sequence (about 24/100/11/9/10/38/20 relative intensity, strongest at 25.85°) matches the simulated Li2CrO2 pattern, and no unexplained peaks suggest a second phase."}
